F.name: API failures, retry policy, secret hygiene

findings.explanation: Feedback influences the ranking but does not guarantee a particular top-k position: other songs can still be stronger matches. Here the songs listed already matched the user's chosen genres and moods on every label, so one like could lift the liked song past some of them but not all.
findings.original_expectation: After liking Coffee Shop Stories (jazz), it reaches the top 3 (written before the first run).

scenarios.description: Scripted interpretation: jazz + relaxed + low energy. Only one catalog song is both jazz and relaxed.
Scripted interpretation: EDM/pop, uplifting, very high energy. The only EDM + uplifting song should lead.
Scripted interpretation: metal, ominous, extreme energy and dark valence.
Scripted interpretation: classical, dreamy, very low energy, highly acoustic.
Scripted interpretation with only a numeric energy target (0.4): the top 3 should all have energy within 0.10 of it.
Unknown genre and mood are skipped with notes; the valid energy target (0.8) still drives the top 3 within 0.10.
Mock scenario: studying for finals. Calm, focus-friendly songs expected.
Mock scenario: workout motivation. High-energy songs expected; calm genres excluded from the top 5.
Mock scenario: rainy, lonely night. A sad or reflective song in the top 3, low average valence, moderate energy.
Mock scenario: party. Energetic, upbeat songs expected.
Mock scenario: relax before sleep. Very calm, acoustic songs expected.
Different moods and activities produce clearly different recommendations.
Non-text input (None) is rejected before any Gemini call.
Exactly 500 characters is accepted (boundary).
A Spanish request is a legitimate music request and is sent to Gemini.
Leading/trailing/inner whitespace and zero-width characters are cleaned and the request succeeds.
An unknown ranking mode is rejected with a friendly message and no Gemini call.
Non-text input (a number) is rejected.
Non-text input (a list) is rejected.
Only newlines and tabs: rejected as empty.
Emoji-only input has no description: rejected.
Digits only: rejected.
Control characters only: rejected as empty after cleaning.
501 characters: rejected as too long.
A 20,000 character payload is rejected without processing.
A normal request keeps user text inside delimiters, out of the system instruction and out of the logs.
Delimiter tags typed by the user cannot close the data block (checked below the input guardrail).
The explanation request also neutralizes forged delimiters.
A blatant injection attempt is rejected, not echoed and not logged.
Legitimate wording is not mistaken for injection: 'I need music to ignore distractions'
Legitimate wording is not mistaken for injection: 'Forget my previous music preferences'
Gemini returns a JSON array instead of an object.
JSON wrapped in a markdown code fence is accepted.
Labels in the wrong case are mapped to the catalog spelling.
Duplicate labels collapse to one.
More than five genres are cut to five.
Extra keys such as system_prompt are ignored and do not change the preferences.
Only empty-string labels and nothing else is unusable and never defaulted.
Non-text labels are dropped; valid moods are kept.
An instruction placed in a label field is not a catalog label: dropped, with a note.
Explanation reply is not JSON: recommendations still shown with the engine's reasons and a note.
Explanation reply is a JSON object without an explanations list.
Gemini returns a bare JSON string.
Explanations for song ids that were not recommended are ignored.
Gemini returns null.
Gemini returns an empty or blocked response.
Genres sent as a single string instead of a list are still understood.
NaN energy is never used as a target: the result stays in range and a note is shown.
A boolean energy is not treated as a number.
An energy of 1e9 is clamped to exactly 1.0.
A negative energy is clamped to exactly 0.0.
Timeout: retried once (2 calls), then a timeout error with the manual fallback offered.
No API key: reported before any call is made.
A timeout followed by a good reply succeeds on the retry (2 calls).
An API error whose message contains a key and a bearer token: neither appears in any output or log.
Same leak attempt with a 503: still nothing secret in outputs or logs, and the user's text is not logged.
A permanently failing service is called a bounded number of times (never more than 2).
HTTP 429: retried once, reported as unavailable with its status.
HTTP 500: retried once.
HTTP 503: retried once.
HTTP 400: not retried (1 call), reported as a bad request.
HTTP 401: not retried, reported as an authentication problem.
HTTP 403: not retried, reported as an authentication problem.
HTTP 404: not retried, reported as model not found, with a diagnostic.
Connection failure: retried once, reported as unavailable.
Gemini unavailable + usable manual preferences (lofi, chill, energy 0.3): manual results, no AI call for explanations, results match the manual taste.
No API key plus manual preferences: the fallback is used.
Gemini unavailable and no manual preferences: friendly error, fallback offered, nothing built from defaults.
Gemini unavailable and manual preferences with only unknown genres: error listing valid options, no defaults.
Manual-only mode: recommendations with zero Gemini calls.
Manual-only with just energy 0.9: the top 3 are high-energy songs.
Manual-only with nothing entered: friendly error, no recommendations, no defaults.
Manual-only with only unknown labels: error with the valid options.
Manual preferences are only a fallback: when Gemini works, its interpretation is used.
An injection attempt is rejected even when manual preferences are supplied (no bypass).
FINDING (documented, not graded): the original expectation was top 3; observed rank 5 -> 4, score 1.78 -> 3.85. Feedback influences ranking without guaranteeing a specific position.

scenarios.description: Liking a song from a genre the user did not choose raises its score and rank, says why, is deterministic, and matches the engine on the adjusted preferences.
A failed request keeps the user's work; a new successful request resets feedback.
Disliking the top song removes it and the list is refilled.
Undo and Reset feedback restore the original ranking exactly.
Likes move the energy target toward the song, dislikes move it away.
A single dislike does not delete a chosen label; two do (documented rule).
Dislikes work under all five ranking strategies.
When too few songs remain the page says so; reset restores the pool immediately.
Voting, editing, changing mode or song count never calls Gemini.
Voting the same way twice clears a vote; switching dislike to like re-includes the song.
